notes: Kept the accepted alignment unchanged in structure and heads; the only edit is an expanded note on s007 recording the two competing readings and why each was rejected, per rule 16.

All 10 source ids and all 17 target ids are partitioned exactly once. Every unit is `aligned`; there are no unrepresented, added or noncompositional units, and no verse in this projection is orphaned across a versification seam (rules 37, 97 not in play).

s007 is the one materially contestable unit. *it* has three defensible homes: on the participle as a supplied object (taken), `added` under rule 103, or folded onto the antecedent s003/s004 on the shape of 3JN.1.13. Rule 74 states in terms that a supplied object stays with the verb that requires it in English, and rule 103 names a resumptive pronoun as its own contrast case, so the taken reading rests on two explicit contract statements rather than on analogy.

s001 has no Greek article, so rule 32's split of a substantival article from its participle is not triggered and rule 90 does not bear on it; the supplied antecedent pronoun and the relativizer both stay with the participle as rule 7 helpers, headed on *knoweth* under rule 17.

The two English *to him* phrases are not a double realization of one token: t001/t002 is the participle's supplied antecedent with the dative case preposition riding along, and t013/t014 is the resumptive `αὐτῷ`. Rule 103's repeated-lexical-content test does not reach them, both being pronouns the ASV writes for distinct source tokens.

s010 keeps the supplied dummy *it* because the Greek copula is expressed; the supplied-copula chain of rules 53/62/63/68/96 governs only verbless clauses and has no application here, so `ἁμαρτία` correctly stands bare on t017.
